main_issue: Whether and how Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling food (fish curry) in the shared kitchen without the smell disturbing A, B and C

A-B.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling cooking (T1); B only described the smell and suggested closing the door (T2), then accepted D's warning plan (T21). B never addressed A's ban, and A never addressed B's plan, so the link is weak.

A-C.evidence: Both complained about the smell (T3, T5). C accepted D's day-based plan (T19) and A accepted the after-7 plan (T11). They never addressed each other directly.

A-D.evidence: A first wanted no strong-smelling cooking at all (T1). A then proposed cooking after 7 (T9), D agreed (T10), and A said 'That works for me' (T11). A gave up the ban and D accepted a timing limit.

B-C.evidence: Both said the smell reaches their space and that after 7 still doesn't help (T12, T13). They each ended up accepting a different accommodation from D (T19, T21), with no direct exchange between them.

B-D.evidence: B said the smell still reaches the room at any evening hour (T18). D said 'I don't know what else I can do' (T20). B proposed a warning before cooking (T21) and D agreed (T25). B accepted the cooking and D accepted the warning duty.

C-D.evidence: C said the laundry smell remained after 7 (T13) and gave the laundry days (T15). D offered to avoid Monday, Wednesday and Friday (T16), and C accepted (T19). D made the move.
